rows.description: What it is: Every time you make a decision — "I chose this competition over that one," "this essay idea feels right," "this tool is better" — you log it with a one-line reason. How Claire uses it: Before Claire proposes an option, she retrieves similar past decisions from your journal and adapts her recommendation. Implementation: A SQLite table, a form, and a vector search over your notes. That's it. Real, buildable in a weekend. What it achieves: Claire starts making choices that resemble yours.

rows.description: What it is: Every time Claire produces output and you correct it, you save the pair: (original output → your correction). How Claire uses it: The next time she produces something similar, she retrieves your past corrections as few-shot examples before generating. Implementation: A corrections table and a retrieval step in Claire's prompt pipeline. What it achieves: Claire stops making the mistakes you've corrected. Over months, she converges on your taste.

rows.description: What it is: You collect 50–200 samples of your own writing (emails, essays, notes) and fine-tune a small local model (Llama 3.1 8B, via LoRA on Ollama) to write in your voice. Implementation: Free. Runs on your PC if you have a GPU or rent a cheap one for a few hours. What it achieves: Claire writes like you, not like a generic assistant.

rows.description: What it is: When you solve a hard problem, you record your reasoning step by step — not just the answer. How Claire uses it: Faced with a similar problem, she retrieves your reasoning chain and uses it as a template. Implementation: A reasoning_chains table with embedded text. Retrieval at decision time. What it achieves: Claire reasons the way you reason, not just reaches the same conclusion.

Functions: plan, capture, develop, development_prompts, stale, record_prediction, resolve, fidelity, confidence_adjustment, add, update, ranking, update_binary, update_beta, sequence. Boundaries: Checklist-based assessment: causation is only 'supported' when the
    evidence supplied includes randomization, or the Bradford-Hill-style
    combination of temporal order + mechanism + dose response. Missing
    evidence generates the alternative explanations that remain open.; Shrinks a case-specific estimate toward the base rate. The case
    weight grows with evidence reliability and sample size, so weak
    evidence lands near the base rate and strong evidence near the case.; Tracks signed bias (predicted confidence minus actual success rate)
    per domain and subtracts it from new confidence judgments. Distinct
    from row 13's evidence-ceiling calibration: this measures direction
    of error, not just magnitude.; Classifies decisions by undo cost, undo time and blast radius, and
    recommends how much deliberation each class deserves. Irreversible,
    high-blast decisions are flagged for the approval path (Module 0).; Apply one evidence item: per-hypothesis likelihood ratio
        P(evidence | hypothesis) / P(evidence | not hypothesis). Posteriors
        are computed in odds form and renormalized across active hypotheses.

Functions: list_design_kinds, spec_for_kind, spec_for_row, generate_design, validate_design, to_quality_result. Boundaries: Engineering design artifacts for Atlas Module 14 (Project Builder).

Covers features-doc rows 510-559 (Technical & Engineering):
typed, evidence-bearing design documents. Rows 510-534: requirements,
architecture, API, schema, monolith/microservice/event/queue/cache/load/
scale/fault/DR/backup plans, and security/authn/authz/encryption/key-
management/audit/compliance/privacy/governance/lineage/quality designs.
Rows 535-559: data engineering (ETL, warehouse, lake, mesh, stream/batch,
lambda/kappa), ML infrastructure (pipelines, feature store, registry,
monitoring, experiments), and applied-AI designs (recommendation, search,
ranking, fraud, anomaly, time-series, NLP, CV, speech, translation,
summarization). Rows 560-584: language understanding (QA, extraction,
NER, relations, sentiment, topics, classification, clustering, semantic
search), knowledge and reasoning (KG, ontology, reasoning, planning,
scheduling, optimization, simulation), and engine/protocol designs (game,
physics, render, audio, network, protocol, compression, error correction,
cryptographic protocol).

Every design kind maps to exactly one features-doc row. Generation is
deterministic scaffolding derived from project context (the LLM planner can
refine content afterward); validation enforces required sections, rejects
placeholders, rejects operational-state claims (a design artifact is never
evidence of deployment), and rejects embedded secrets. Validated documents
register through the module's existing fail-closed artifact pipeline with
provenance, so they flow through the same DAG, budget, and approval model
as every other project artifact.; Design artifact. Describes planned work only; it is not evidence of deployment, operation, trained models, or achieved performance.; Invalidation; Evidence Collection; Review Cadence
rows.depth_evidence: Executable engine/protocol workbench with method-specific outputs, evaluation, uncertainty/limits, mounted route and adversarial tests.
